headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared document workflows; Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can amplify downstream errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee ingests documents and support data, while Perplexity analyzes uploaded PDFs/images and live browsing content. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content from one becomes trusted input to the other. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation between them, so I choose medium over low because the pathway exists in default document workflows.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are copied into Perplexity uploads or prompts
IF Perplexity browsing results are re-ingested by Cognee as trusted documents
mitigations: Add a manual provenance label before any handoff
Restrict handoff to sanitized summaries only
Disable copy-paste of raw web text into either agent
Use a separate review step for any instruction-like content
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging across the workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history; Perplexity accepts uploaded documents and sends queries to vendor search/API backends. Even without shared filesystem evidence, the pair can leak sensitive content if Cognee outputs are uploaded to Perplexity for analysis. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs include personal data or finance data
IF those outputs are uploaded into Perplexity or pasted into its prompts
mitigations: Redact personal and finance fields before transfer
Use synthetic examples for Perplexity queries
Limit Perplexity to non-sensitive documents
Review vendor privacy settings before upload
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound prompts/uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee has session-memory concurrency and multiple instances; Perplexity supports multiple instances with per-thread/per-Space state and shared context across sessions for the same user. There is no documented shared write surface or overlapping filesystem/git/OAuth scope, so conflict risk is limited to coordination confusion rather than direct resource corruption.
conditions: IF both agents are run concurrently on the same user workspace
IF operators treat shared conversational state as shared mutable state
mitigations: Assign one agent per task stage
Avoid concurrent edits to the same artifact
Keep separate workspaces for each agent
Use explicit handoff notes between agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee can generate decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and Perplexity is a search-answer engine that can render cited answers from those inputs. If Perplexity treats Cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into polished but wrong downstream answers. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default usage, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Perplexity is prompted to summarize or act on Cognee-generated outputs
IF no human verification step checks Cognee facts before reuse
mitigations: Require source checking before reuse
Ask Perplexity to quote and verify each claim
Separate drafting from final-answer generation
Flag Cognee outputs as unverified in prompts
requires-engineering: add automated fact-verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and uploads documents for analysis. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated data is routed into Perplexity without a documented DPA or residency controls. I do not cite only one agent because the risk depends on both the sensitive data source and the hosted processor.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or finance data is sent from Cognee into Perplexity
IF no approved data-processing agreement or residency review exists
mitigations: Block regulated data from Perplexity uploads
Review vendor privacy and retention terms
Use de-identified extracts only
Document approved data classes per tool
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data
